english: "Hear me, father Varuna!"
uncertain: pter: unreduced spelling of ph₂ter (voc.), not in analyzer
werune: vocative of a god-name Werunos (Varuna); not in lexicon
moi: enclitic gen/dat 'me' (object of hearing)

english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the field.
uncertain: tat/kukruwants/awis/agram/ā/bʰugat: old (Schleicher-style) orthography, none analyzed; read as tód 'this', perfect participle of ḱlew- 'having heard', h₂ówis 'sheep', h₂éǵrom 'field', ā 'to/into', bʰug- 'fled'

english: O Sky and Earth, hear my words. I have taken this young woman as wife. I shall not leave her. I shall protect her, I shall work for her, and I shall give her butter. She shall not go thirsty. I shall build a fence for her. If I strike her, may the thunder strike me, and may my horses not carry me.
uncertain: ḱlutóm: read as IMP.2DU 'hear (you two)', addressed to Sky and Earth; could also be adj. 'famous'
h₁áyh₂e: MID.AOR.1SG 'I took/received'
térseti: SBJV.3SG of 'become thirsty'
h₁yód: read as conjunction 'if'
misfit: gʷʰn̥yéh₁s: OPT.2SG ('may you strike'), but its subject gʰrómos 'thunder' is nominative 3sg (not vocative gʰróme); expected 3sg gʷʰn̥yéh₁t, as in 04ee203f

english: Father Sky and Mother Earth, hear us two. We two chiefs have sworn this oath, drunk this water, and join ourselves together. I shall not drive off your horses, and you shall not drive off my sheep. Whoever breaks this oath, may the thunder strike him and may his fields not bear. May wolves devour him. Whoever keeps this oath, may he grow rich in livestock.
uncertain: dʰh₁wé: AOR.1DU 'we (two) placed/made' (the oath)
yungwósdʰh₂: MID.PRS.1DU 'we join ourselves'; present, while the verbs before it are aorist
dʰugʰih₁ént: OPT.3PL, read as dʰewgʰ- 'be productive'; the homonym 'hit, meet' does not fit
péḱesh₁: INS.SG of péḱos 'livestock, wealth' (lexicon gives no gloss)

english: O chief, you are gone, and death has seized you. Now who protects us? You used to give us gold and wool, and you guarded our fields. Now clouds cover the sun. The light has vanished, and your horses do not eat. Grief is in our hearts. Sleep does not come to us. We sit by your wall. We remember you, and your fame is great.
uncertain: h₁épt: AOR.3SG 'seized' (also possible: PST of a present h₁épti)
dédeh₃s / péh₂s: PST.2SG, past ongoing ('used to give', 'guarded')
nos: acc/gen/dat; 'to us' with dédeh₃s, 'our' with h₂éǵrons
dʰéyǵʰesi: LOC.SG 'at the wall' (also SBJV.2SG of a verb, which does not fit)
misfit: h₂éh₂usoh₁: instrumental 'with gold' joined by -kʷe to the accusative object h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m of dédeh₃s; expected accusative h₂éh₂usom (unless 'endowed us with gold' was meant)

english: O man, wake up! You lie in the field. You do not hear us, and your head has gone cold. Your swift horses stand by the chariot. You were free and did not fear the serpent. You slew the serpent and drove the cattle into your own stall. Your fame is imperishable. Your mother trembles with grief. Your wife sits in the night. Now we carry you to the fire. O Fire, carry this man to the gods.
uncertain: gʷʰéns: PST.2SG (past ongoing) of 'strike, slay', said of a completed feat
h₁és: PST.2SG 'you were' (also AOR of 'throw')
h₁égʷʰis: GEN/ABL, read as ablative of fear
h₁n̥gʷním: accusative of goal 'to the fire', next to object te
misfit: gʷowsth₂ṓs: NOM.PL 'cow-stalls' does not agree with swóm (ACC.SG) and cannot be the goal of h₁élh₂s; expected ACC.SG gʷowsth₂óm (compare 47667062 swóm gʷowsth₂óm h₁élh₂m̥)

english: The chief was yoking four horses to the chariot. He gave me the chariot, and now I drive it. Swift dogs follow it. Men look at me, and I am content. They say: "Who gave you this chariot?" The chief, giver of good things, gave it to me.
uncertain: yunégt: PST.3SG 'was yoking'
h₂éǵoh₂: PRS.1SG 'I drive' (also SBJV.1SG of 'say', which does not fit)
tetórph₂e: PRF.1SG 'I am satisfied'
sékʷontor: MID.PRS.3PL 'follow'

english: I am the chief's praiser. He overcame wolves and guards the boundary. He is mighty, and the wolves fear him. He gave me five horses and wool. The men listen to my song at night. He became famous, and I became famous. Heavenly gods, protect him!
uncertain: stéwtōr: 'praiser' (lexicon entry has no gloss; from root stew- 'praise')
térh₂ut: PST.3SG 'was overcoming'
tósmōd: ABL.SG 'from him', used with 'fear'
bʰúHm̥: AOR.1SG 'I became'; switch to the speaker (the poet shares the fame), no h₁eǵ given
ph₂sté: IMP.2PL (could also be PRS or PST 2PL); read as a command with the vocative

english: You gave me three horses and nine sheep. In return I give you a song. The years go by. The cattle died; the brothers died; the gold vanished. But good fame did not die: you live in my words.
uncertain: h₂m̥bʰí: read as 'in exchange'; could be 'around/about'
wétōs: neuter plural with singular verb h₁éyti, the normal rule for neuter plurals
h₁ési: PRS.2SG 'you are' (in my words)

english: The chief died in the night, and the birds flew away. The moon did not shine. Then at dawn the men carried him to the fire. The fire burned him. His trembling wife sat in front. His dog did not eat. Then the men praised his deeds. They set his name in a song. Then they built a wall around him. O chief, your name is imperishable.
uncertain: tóm: masc. ACC 'him' (the chief); péh₂wr̥ is neuter, so tóm cannot modify it. péh₂wr̥ is read as an accusative of goal in sentence 3 and as subject in sentence 4
litént: AOR.3PL of 'go away' (also 'touch', which does not fit)
h₂énti: adverb 'in front' (also LOC of 'forehead')
bʰéront/h₁érkʷont/démont: PST.3PL, past ongoing

english: Daughter, go to your husband's house. May you be mistress there. May your husband's mother and sister come to love you, and may his brothers love you. At dawn, get up, carry water, and prepare the fire. Work at the quern, and may your heart not grow weary. Learn your husband's household work. May you not fear his brothers. Your husband is a true man. Young woman, do not tremble. May you see the sons of your sons, and may the gods protect you.
uncertain: dʰéh₁mn̥: 'house, home' (one of several senses); accusative of goal
wn̥Hih₁tā́m: OPT.3DU, agrees with the two subjects mother + sister
mē tréms: mē + augmentless past 2sg read as a prohibition
dayh₂urbʰós: ABL.PL with 'fear'

english: Great chief, you lie in your own house, you who gave us horses as gifts, who slew wolves, who guarded our boundary. Now sleep has taken you. We warm water for you and lay you out. Your brothers stand around you. Your sisters sit at your head. Your chariot stands still: now who will drive it? May your famous name not perish.
uncertain: dʰh₁méni: LOC 'in the house'
dóh₃r̥h₂: neuter pl. 'as gifts', in apposition to h₁éḱwons
supnós: 'sleep' or 'death', both senses listed
tn̥numés: 'we stretch (you) out', read as laying out the body
h₂éǵeti: PRS.3SG 'drives' (SBJV of 'say' does not fit)

english: My song, stand up and go to the lord. Speak to him at dawn: "Your praiser praises you. You gave him two chariots and seven piglets. He does not go thirsty. Your name is famous." Do not grow weary on the lord's road.
uncertain: kéh₂nmn̥: vocative; the song is addressed
tósmey ... déh₃s: 'you gave to him', 'him' meaning the praiser, spoken of in the 3rd person; where the quoted speech begins and ends is my reading
dwóh₁ Hroth₂óh₁: ACC.DU 'two chariots' (INS.SG also possible)
h₁érkʷeti: from root h₁erkʷ- 'praise' (lexicon entry has no gloss)

english: I came to the lord and spoke new words. Then, sitting by the fire, he listened. Then he stood up and recognized me. He gave me seven cows and a horse. I drove them into my own stall, and my heart rejoiced. May the chief's fame be imperishable.
uncertain: néweh₂: neuter pl. 'new', agreeing with wékʷōs; -kʷe placed on the adjective
ǵnéh₃t: 'got to know, recognized'
tóns: masc. ACC.PL 'them' (cows + horse)

english: Who gave me these four horses? The chief gave them to me as gifts. I brought three wagons; they were filled with gold. I drove them along the road, and men saw me. I praise him whose gifts are great. May he live and may he not grow weary.
uncertain: tóns ... dóh₃r̥h₂: tóns is masc. ACC.PL and does not agree with neuter dóh₃r̥h₂, so read as 'them (the horses) as gifts'
h₁opéyom: PST.1SG of 'make reach; give'. Read as 'I brought', but 'I gave' would clash with the speaker being the one who receives; elsewhere this verb means 'give' (h₁opéyet, h₁opéyes)
pl̥nh₁n̥tó: MID.PST.3PL 'were filled'; finite verb in asyndeton, with no nominative subject
ǵʰḗm: AOR.1SG, read as ǵʰeyt- 'drive on'; ǵʰew- 'pour' does not fit

english: O chief, I trust you, and I have sworn my oath. Sky and Earth are listening. I shall follow you and stand before you. I shall not stray from the path. I shall guard your gifts and keep watch at your fence. If I leave you, may my name perish and may dogs and birds devour me.
uncertain: bʰebʰóydʰh₂e: PRF.1SG 'I trust'
ḱléwsetes: PRS.2DU or 3DU; read as 3DU with the nominatives
pró: preverb 'before'
h₃sléydʰoh₂: SBJV.1SG 'slip, stray'

english: Husband, you have left me. The fire of your house does not burn. Your dog looks for you, and I tremble. Your sons are young. Now who will lead them, and who will plough? Your harrow lies by the wall. How did you fall? Guarding the sheep, you fell at the boundary. Your field is red with blood. May men hear of your good fame. I shall not marry again. Husband, I remember you.
uncertain: kʷíh₁: analyzer gives only dual; read as instrumental 'how?'
linékʷs: PST.2SG 'you were leaving'
h₂éryēti: SBJV.3SG 'shall plough'
snéwbʰōh₂: SBJV.1SG of 'marry' (from root snewbʰ-; lexicon entry has no gloss)

english: The horse said: "Listen, sheep! It pains our heart to see man, the master, make the sheep's wool into a warm garment for himself, while the sheep have no wool."
uncertain: ewewkʷ/h₂gʰnutoy/widntbʰós/dʰǵʰémōn/h₂wlnéh₂m/kʷnewti/sébʰoy/gʷʰérmom/h₂wlh₂néh₂: different reconstruction orthography, not analyzed. Read as 'said', 'pains', 'to (us) seeing', 'man', 'wool', 'makes', 'for himself', 'warm', 'wool'
h₂ówyom: read as GEN.PL 'of sheep'; the analyzer offers 'egg', which does not fit
h₁éḱwōs: analyzer gives NOM.PL; the verb ewewkʷ is unanalyzed, so number cannot be checked. Translated as singular because the fable has one speaking horse
h₂wlnéh₂m / h₂wlh₂néh₂: wool is spelled two ways within the item, and both differ from the lexicon's h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂
h₂éwibʰoskʷe: DAT.PL of possession ('the sheep have'), not the singular sheep addressed

english: The chief brings me gifts in the mornings. Yesterday he heard my song, and his heart rejoiced. Now he has given me six cows and nine sheep. They built a stall for them. I am a knower of words. He knows me and I know him. Now my name is famous. His fame is imperishable.
uncertain: h₂usú: LOC.PL 'at dawns, in the mornings'
démont: PST.3PL with no stated subject ('they built'); tóybʰos DAT.PL 'for them' (the animals)

english: Two brothers gave me gifts. They gave ten horses and four wagons. The horses are swift. The wagons carry wool. Their gifts are great. I praise both of them, and their sisters. May their fame spread far.
uncertain: tóysōm: plural genitive used for the two brothers, where a dual would be expected
h₁áytām: AOR.3DU (also IMP.3DU)
tetn̥yéh₁t: OPT.3SG 'be stretched, extend'

english: The gods gave the chief wealth in livestock. He gives it to me. He gave three horses, nine cows, and a stall. For him I make a new song. I am his praiser. May my words be sweet to him. O Agni, hear my words. May he live and not grow weary.
uncertain: péḱos: 'livestock, wealth' (lexicon has no gloss; root péḱ- 'wealth'); tód agrees with it (neuter)
suh₂dyéh₁t: OPT.3SG; neuter plural wékʷōs with singular verb

english: Daughter, you are leaving your mother. Go with your own husband. Your husband carries you off. Daughter, put on your shoes. Do not fear the road. May your road be passable and may your husband's brothers lead you. Wear the wool that I gave you. Remember me, and I shall remember you. May Dawn, daughter of Sky, shine for you, and may your heart rejoice.
uncertain: h₂uHsó: MID.IMP.2SG 'put on (footwear)'; no object given
mē bʰéyh₂s: mē + aorist injunctive, a prohibition
wéso: MID.IMP.2SG 'wear' (MID.PST.3SG also possible)

english: This butter melts in the fire. Whoever breaks this oath, may he melt like it. This wool burns in the fire. Whoever breaks this oath, may his house burn. This water boils. Whoever breaks this oath, may his blood boil. The Sun has seen him, and Sky hears him.
uncertain: tóm (final sentence): masc. ACC; read as 'him' (the oath-breaker). It cannot be the oath (feminine tā́m) or the rite (neuter tód)
h₁éwsetor: MID.PRS.3SG 'burns'
dʰéh₁mn̥: 'house' among the listed senses

english: My son, where are you? You lie down, and night covers you. Your forehead has gone cold, and you were young. I nourished you and carried you about. You were growing up, but you did not become a man. Who seized you? Death seized you in the night. Mother Earth, guard him.
uncertain: ní ḱéyth₂er: 'lie down'
h₂élom/bʰoréyom: PST.1SG, past ongoing
upó bʰuHyés: 'you were growing up'
tóm: shifts to 3rd person 'him' in the prayer to Earth

english: The great chief is gone. The giver of gold is gone. The lord of horses is gone. O chief, you were our sun; you have gone down, and now night has come. To me, your praiser, you gave ten horses. Now who will give me gifts? Who will listen to my words? I make a new song for you. It carries you to the gods.
uncertain: séngʷs: AOR.2SG 'sank, went down' (of the sun)
stutréy: DAT.SG of stéwtōr 'praiser'
márkons: 'horses' (a different horse word)
bʰéreti: PRS.3SG 'carries'; 'it carries you to the gods' is the literal reading

english: Let us praise this great man. He saved the cattle from the wolves and did not fear death. His heart has gone cold, and his dog lies beside him. Let us lift him and lay him down. Let us place gold at his head. Let us remember his deeds. O man, go on the path of the fathers; pass by the two dogs, and may the fathers receive you.
uncertain: mr̥téys: GEN/ABL, read as ablative with 'fear'
dʰgʷʰh₂dʰí: IMP.2SG 'come near, pass by'
h₁áyih₁ro: MID.OPT.3PL 'may they receive'

english: The young husband was yoking two swift horses to the wagon, and he drove to the young woman's house. Wearing new wool, she was standing by the wall. Her brother led her out and seated her in the wagon. Then the husband drove the two away, and his brothers followed her. The road was passable and they did not slip. A bird sat on the fence and gave a sign. The husband's sister received her at the fire. The young men were drinking and were joyful. The brothers-in-law were cooking a piglet. May the gods give them good things.
uncertain: tóh₁: masc. dual, read as the two horses
séh₂ (bird sentence): feminine 'she/it', read as the bird (could be the bride)
séh₂gyet: 'seek out, give a sign' (omen)

english: Yesterday the father gave his own daughter to the husband, and the husband gave the bride-price: four horses and a wagon. Her mother clothed her in new wool, and her sister set a comb on her head. Then the husband led her from her house, and her two brothers walked behind. Then they reached the husband's enclosure. The husband led her three times around the fire, and his brother seated her by the fire. The brothers-in-law looked at her and were astonished. Then the husband said: "I am Sky, you are Earth." Then she stepped onto the millstone. O Agni, protect this wife. May sons and daughters be born to her, and may she live with her husband. May death not reach her.
uncertain: dʰh₁méns: ABL 'from her house'
h₁ludʰónt: AOR.3PL with no stated subject ('they arrived')
stéygʰet: PST.3SG with no stated subject, read as the bride
pótih₁: INS.SG 'with the husband'
